headline: This removes an old, unused profile-picture field from the user records. It is safe to ship.
what_changed: Removes an old field that held a web link to each user's profile picture. It belongs to the old picture system.
Adds a change to how the database is organised (a migration). When it is published, it deletes that old field from the users table.
Users should notice nothing. Profile pictures already come from the newer picture system, and that is not changed.

risks.title: Undo brings back the field but not its old contents
risks.explanation: After publishing, the old picture links are deleted for good. If someone undoes the change, the field comes back empty. This matters very little. The links were copied to the new system in April, and they stopped working when the old image host shut down in May. A normal database backup before publishing covers any remaining worry.

questions_for_developer: Is there any other system that still reads the old picture-link field straight from the database, such as reports, a data warehouse or another company's tool? I checked this app's own code only.
good_news: I searched the app. Nothing reads or writes the old field any more. Profile pictures are built only from the newer field.
The database change has an undo step, and it links correctly to the earlier database changes.
The change is small and tidy. It removes clutter that nothing uses.
